record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Boundary-condition dependence for discrete-delay memory model
record.original_question: For the discrete-delay scalar movement model ∂_t u = d1Δu − γ∇·(u∇u_τ) + f(u), where u_τ means the population density τ time units in the past and f is logistic-type growth, how does the existing analysis change if one replaces the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition by periodic or homogeneous Dirichlet boundary data?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 23. In [72], a homogeneous Neumann boundary condition is chosen for model (2.20). How does the analysis performed in [72] change with respect to changes in boundary data, such as a periodic boundary condition or homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the scalar reaction–diffusion equation with a discrete temporal delay modelling animal movement with memory:
  ∂_t u(x,t) = d_1 Δu(x,t) − γ ∇·( u(x,t) ∇u(x,t−τ) ) + f(u(x,t)),  x ∈ Ω, t > 0,
where Ω ⊂ R^n is a bounded smooth domain, d_1 > 0 is the diffusion coefficient, γ ∈ R is a memory-induced advection coefficient, τ > 0 is a fixed time delay, u(x,t−τ) represents the population density τ time units in the past, and f is a logistic-type growth nonlinearity (for example f(u) = r u (1 − u/K) with r, K > 0). An initial history u(x,s) = u_0(x,s), s ∈ [−τ,0], is prescribed.

The existing analysis (well-posedness, stability of constant steady states, linearised dispersion relation, Hopf and Turing-type bifurcation thresholds in (γ,τ)-parameter space, and the nature of bifurcating spatiotemporal patterns) has been carried out under the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition
  ∂u/∂ν = 0 on ∂Ω × (0,∞).

Problem. Determine how the well-posedness theory, the linear stability of homogeneous equilibria, the location and type of bifurcations (Turing, Hopf, Turing–Hopf), and the resulting pattern-formation behaviour for the above model change when the homogeneous Neumann condition is replaced by:
 (a) periodic boundary conditions (Ω = T^n a flat torus), or
 (b) homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions u = 0 on ∂Ω × (0,∞).
In each case, identify the admissible eigenfunctions of the underlying Laplacian, derive the corresponding characteristic equation for perturbations of constant (or, in the Dirichlet case, non-constant) equilibria, and describe how the bifurcation structure and emergent patterns depend on the choice of boundary data.
artifact.status_search_result: No published work was located that carries out the analysis of this discrete-delay memory-advection model under periodic or homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions; existing analyses are restricted to homogeneous Neumann data. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Delay partial differential equations - Scholarpedia
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses parabolic delay PDEs and spectral/bifurcation analysis but does not treat the memory-advection model u_t = dΔu − γ∇·(u∇u_τ) + f(u) under Dirichlet or periodic data.
status_evidence.claim: No analysis of the specific model under non-Neumann boundary conditions is reported.

status_evidence.title: Delayed Parabolic Regularity
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys regularity for parabolic systems with discrete delay but does not address the cognitive-mapping movement model with memory-driven advection.
status_evidence.claim: No treatment of periodic/Dirichlet versions of the memory PDE.
